Onboarding Standard Operating Procedure (HR Department)

All new employees must complete comprehensive orientation within 3 business days of joining Precision Textile Industry Limited. Required steps include: 1) Document submission to HRIS system including emergency contacts and bank details, 2) Completion of mandatory security and safety training modules, 3) Department-specific orientation with direct supervisor, 4) IT equipment provisioning and system access setup. Managers are responsible for creating a detailed 30/60/90 day performance plan and scheduling regular check-ins. HR will conduct follow-up interviews at 30 and 90 days to ensure successful integration.

Letter of Credit Policy (Finance Department)

All Letters of Credit exceeding 50,000 USD require dual approval from Finance Director and Chief Operating Officer. Pre-shipment inspection: All export shipments must have confirmed LC terms before release from warehouse. Discrepancy management: Any LC discrepancies must be reported to the issuing bank within 48 hours of document presentation. Documentation requirements: Commercial invoice, packing list, bill of lading, and certificate of origin must match LC terms exactly. Payment terms: LC sight drafts are processed within 5 business days upon compliant document presentation. Beneficiary banks: Only work with pre-approved correspondent banks for LC negotiations.

Production Quality Standards for Textile Operations

Quality control checkpoints: Fabric inspection at 3 stages - incoming raw materials, post-dyeing, and final finishing. MHM embroidery machine maintenance: Daily calibration checks and weekly deep cleaning protocols. Color matching standards: All production batches must match approved color standards within Delta E < 2.0 tolerance. Defect classification: Grade A (export quality) allows maximum 2 minor defects per 100 square meters. Customer specifications: RB Knit, Blue Planet Knitwear, and Fiat Fashion have specific quality parameters documented in QC-2024 manual. Rejection protocols: Any batch exceeding defect limits requires supervisor approval and rework documentation.
